## Behaviour
Explicit reads attach `text_findings` listing each affected source (`title`, `body`, `comment` with index and author, `label`), as sparse objects `{"source": "body", "zero_width": true}`. Human output appends a bracketed note on the row (`[title: contains confusable characters; body: contains zero-width characters]`) or a `text findings:` block in `show` with `comment 2 (@author)`. Items with no findings carry no `text_findings` key and no bracket. Text is shown as is (never rewritten), but control characters are replaced when printed in a terminal row.

## Scenarios
- golden: triage of one item with a confusable title and a zero-width body shows both findings with sources in JSON and in the row note; an item with a ZWJ family emoji shows none. Prevents reviewers missing hidden text and crying wolf on emoji.
- golden: show of an item whose comment carries a bidi control names `comment 1 (@author)` in human output. Prevents attributing a finding to the wrong field.
- adversary: a tag-character payload not spelling a subdivision flag in a title is reported as `unicode_tags`. Prevents hidden payloads.

## Reference coverage
Reference read-suite walks: triage attributes pinned findings without flagging emoji; flags tag sequences; show attributes comment findings in JSON and human output (3 tests).
